about: T9.28's presentation video: the script the owner approved on 2026-11-09 (draft 1, with changes the owner approved the same day: after code review round 1, the clients scene's sentence on the audit log and Piper's licence in the credits as GPL-3.0-or-later; after compliance run 1, the app's own log lines in the last scene and USDA FoodData Central in the credits; then the opening calls it a personal portfolio project, without naming a course). Each scene shows a title card or the demo's screenshots; 'shows' pairs a screenshot with the sentence it starts at. The sentences are the narration and the subtitles. scripts/make_video.py builds the video from it; tests/test_video_script.py checks what it must and must not say.

card: A coach-first workspace with an AI agent
Demo mode: made-up users and data. Synthetic voice.
narration: This is Fitcoach AI Assistant, a personal portfolio project.
You are hearing a synthetic voice.
Everything you see runs locally, in the app's demo mode, with made-up users and data.

card: Coaches collect logs by hand and answer the same questions
Clients get advice with no source behind it
narration: Coaches who work with recreational lifters spend a lot of time collecting what their clients eat and train, and answering the same nutrition questions.
Clients often get advice with no source behind it.
Fitcoach gives the coach one workspace.
Clients log their own food, weight and workouts.
An AI agent answers from open-licensed sports nutrition research.
And the coach stays in charge of what the client is told.
Here the demo coach asks how much protein a day helps build muscle.
The answer is written by an AI model.
The agent first decides whether to search the research at all.
Here it searches, and the answer cites the passages it used, as S1, S2 and so on.
Under Sources, each cited article is listed with its authors, year, journal and licence.
When the sources do not cover a question, the app says so instead of guessing.
The chat also has tools for personal numbers, such as energy needs, macro targets and the nutrients of a food.
On the Clients page, the coach sees each client's week at a glance, with a flag for whom to follow up.
The client decides what to share: body data, nutrition, training, or nothing.
That rule is checked in the data store itself, not only on the page, and when the coach opens a client's data, the read is recorded in a log that the client can see too.
Client week shows one client's logged days, calories against the target, and macros, from what the client shares.
At the end of a week, the coach asks the agent to draft a weekly review.
The agent reads the week's numbers and the research, then stops and waits.
The draft is made by an AI model, and it goes nowhere until the coach approves, edits or rejects it.
The client sees a review only after the coach has approved it.
Now the demo client.
Clients have no AI chat.
On Today they log food from the USDA food table, and their weight.
My week shows the same week, with the approved review, labelled as an AI draft approved by the coach.
Notifications say what changed, such as an approved review, without repeating its text.

card: App logs with no personal data
narration: Under the hood, it is a LangGraph agent with tool calling, hybrid search over open-licensed research articles, input guards against prompt injection, and domain guardrails such as a calorie floor.
The app's own log lines hold no personal data, and its answers are evaluated against a committed baseline.
It is built with Python, LangChain and Streamlit.

card: General information for healthy adults. Not medical advice.
narration: Fitcoach gives general information for healthy adults.
It is not medical advice.
The code and the documentation are on GitHub.
Thanks for watching.

card: Narration: a synthetic voice made offline with Piper text-to-speech (GPL-3.0-or-later), voice en_US-ljspeech (high), trained on the LJ Speech dataset (public domain).
Research sources and USDA FoodData Central data, with their credits and licences: https://github.com/NMH1988/fitcoach-ai-assistant/blob/main/ATTRIBUTION.md
